headline: Massachusetts launches public database for hot-work violations
dek: The state fire service says the searchable system will track enforcement actions involving welding, grinding and other spark-producing work.
body: The Massachusetts Department of Fire Services has launched a public database for violations involving hot-work processes such as welding, grinding and cutting. The agency says the searchable system is intended to make enforcement information available as local fire departments report cases.

The database follows Chapter 114 of the Acts of 2026, which Gov. Maura Healey signed June 26 and which took effect Sept. 26. The law directs the Department of Fire Services to collect information on written notices and fines tied to hot-work violations and maintain a public database with an automated notification system.

The law covers failures to maintain required hot-work training certification, performing hot work without that certification and violations of permit requirements. The fire service says local departments will send information on sanctions, while affected property owners and insurance providers for violators will receive notifications.

The database will be populated over the coming weeks and months as local departments submit enforcement actions, with uploads occurring weekly, according to the Department of Fire Services. The agency cautions that the data is informational and that questions about a particular case should be directed to the fire department identified in the record.

The new system is part of Massachusetts' response to the 2014 nine-alarm fire that killed Boston Fire Lieutenant Edward J. Walsh and Firefighter Michael Kennedy after unpermitted hot work ignited nearby material. Since 2018, people seeking a municipal hot-work permit have been required to show completion of a State Fire Marshal-approved training program, the agency said.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: Massachusetts has launched a public database tracking hot-work violations involving welding, grinding and permit compliance.
